cleanIntro:
The DMK22C is a semi-automatic blowback .22 LR sporting rifle on forged aluminium receivers, built to take AR-15 pattern furniture. It comes apart the AR way: the rear receiver pin pushes out, the upper pivots away from the receiver, and the bolt assembly comes out of the back of the upper. The same book covers the DMK22C and the DMK22C ARCA SWISS; they differ by handguard and muzzle device, not by procedure.

KRISS's interval is a field strip, a clean of the bolt and barrel and a light oil every 400 rounds — sooner in dust and humidity — and a complete teardown, clean and inspection at least every 1,000 rounds. The book itself publishes no procedure past taking the bolt out. One thing it warns against: letting the hammer fall while the upper is off the receiver.

steps.title: Finger outside the guard, safety on
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction for the whole procedure. Take your finger out of the trigger guard and put the safety on before you do anything else.
steps.prose: Every step after this puts your hands near the action. Start from a rifle that cannot fire by a slip.
steps.quote: When finished firing, ALWAYS place your finger outside the trigger guard with the barrel maintained in safe direction and activate the safety.
steps.cite: KRISS DMK Sporting Rifle Series (DMK22C / DMK22C ARCA SWISS) — Owner's Manual — V.01_2023.05.31 — printed on the back page — Unloading and Clearing, printed p.9

steps.title: Magazine out first
steps.action: Press the magazine release and take the magazine out of the well.
steps.prose: Working the charging handle with a magazine still seated only chambers the next round.
steps.quote: Press the magazine release to remove the magazine.
steps.cite: KRISS DMK Sporting Rifle Series (DMK22C / DMK22C ARCA SWISS) — Owner's Manual — V.01_2023.05.31 — printed on the back page — Unloading and Clearing, printed p.9

steps.title: Charging handle back — and HOLD it
steps.action: Pull the charging handle fully to the rear and keep holding it there. Any round in the chamber comes out of the ejection port.
steps.prose: Holding it back keeps the chamber open for the look that comes next.
steps.quote: Pull the charging handle back and hold to the rear.
steps.cite: KRISS DMK Sporting Rifle Series (DMK22C / DMK22C ARCA SWISS) — Owner's Manual — V.01_2023.05.31 — printed on the back page — Unloading and Clearing, printed p.9

steps.title: LOOK into the chamber, then let go — and SAFE
steps.action: Still holding the handle back, look into the chamber and see it empty. Only then release the charging handle and switch the rifle to Safe. Empty every round out of the magazine before it goes anywhere near the rifle again.
steps.prose: Hearing a round drop is not the check; seeing the empty chamber is.
steps.quote: Visually inspect the chamber to confirm it is clear of any ammunition. Release the charging handle.
steps.cite: KRISS DMK Sporting Rifle Series (DMK22C / DMK22C ARCA SWISS) — Owner's Manual — V.01_2023.05.31 — printed on the back page — Unloading and Clearing, printed p.9

steps.title: Charging handle once more — confirm unloaded
steps.action: Magazine still out. Pull the charging handle once more to be sure the rifle is unloaded, and let it go forward.
steps.prose: The book opens its field strip by repeating the clear: the magazine out and the chamber empty before any pin moves.
steps.caution: Check to ensure that the magazine has been removed and that chamber is cleared.
steps.quote: Pull the charging handle to ensure that the firearm is unloaded.
steps.cite: KRISS DMK Sporting Rifle Series (DMK22C / DMK22C ARCA SWISS) — Owner's Manual — V.01_2023.05.31 — printed on the back page — Field Strip, printed p.11

steps.title: Selector on SAFE
steps.action: Set the fire selector switch to Safe and leave it there until the rifle is back together.
steps.prose: Do not work the trigger from here to reassembly.
steps.quote: Set the fire selector switch to safe.
steps.cite: KRISS DMK Sporting Rifle Series (DMK22C / DMK22C ARCA SWISS) — Owner's Manual — V.01_2023.05.31 — printed on the back page — Field Strip, printed p.11

steps.title: Rear receiver pin out
steps.action: Push out the rear receiver pin.
steps.prose: Only the rear pin comes out; the upper pivots open on the other.
steps.quote: Push out the rear receiver pin.
steps.cite: KRISS DMK Sporting Rifle Series (DMK22C / DMK22C ARCA SWISS) — Owner's Manual — V.01_2023.05.31 — printed on the back page — Field Strip, printed p.11

steps.title: ⚠ Pivot the upper open — hammer stays cocked
steps.action: Pivot the upper away from the receiver. From here until the rifle is back together, do NOT let the hammer fall — no trigger pulls with the upper open.
steps.prose: KRISS warns that releasing the hammer with the upper separated can damage the receiver.
steps.caution: Do not release the hammer when the upper has been separated from the receiver. Doing so could cause damage to the receiver.
steps.quote: Pivot the upper to seperate upper from the receiver.
steps.cite: KRISS DMK Sporting Rifle Series (DMK22C / DMK22C ARCA SWISS) — Owner's Manual — V.01_2023.05.31 — printed on the back page — Field Strip, printed p.12

steps.title: Bolt assembly out the back of the upper
steps.action: Pull the charging handle back to bring the bolt assembly out where you can reach it, and take the bolt assembly out of the rear of the upper.
steps.prose: Note which way up the bolt sits as it comes out — it goes back the same way.
steps.quote: Pull the charging handle to expose the bolt assembly, and remove from the rear of the upper.
steps.cite: KRISS DMK Sporting Rifle Series (DMK22C / DMK22C ARCA SWISS) — Owner's Manual — V.01_2023.05.31 — printed on the back page — Field Strip, printed p.12

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: On the bench: the receiver with its fire control group, the upper with the barrel and charging handle, and the bolt assembly with its recoil spring and guide. That is the whole of KRISS's field strip. DEEP CLEAN carries the book's bolt inspection points, the fire control group oiling, and its stopping point.
steps.prose: Every cleaning step in the book starts from this state.
steps.quote: Field strip the firearm to remove the bolt assembly from the upper receiver.
steps.cite: KRISS DMK Sporting Rifle Series (DMK22C / DMK22C ARCA SWISS) — Owner's Manual — V.01_2023.05.31 — printed on the back page — Cleaning and Inspection — Bolt, printed p.13

deepSteps.title: Bolt: body, face, extractor, recoil spring
deepSteps.action: Clean every surface of the bolt assembly with a lint-free cloth and solvent, paying special attention to four places: the body of the bolt, the bolt face, the extractor, and the recoil spring and guide.
deepSteps.prose: A dirty bolt face and a fouled extractor are on the book's list of causes for failures to feed, seat and extract.
deepSteps.quote: With a lint free cloth and firearms cleaning solution (sold separately), clean all surfaces of the bolt assembly with special attention to:
deepSteps.cite: KRISS DMK Sporting Rifle Series (DMK22C / DMK22C ARCA SWISS) — Owner's Manual — V.01_2023.05.31 — printed on the back page — Cleaning and Inspection — Bolt, printed p.13

deepSteps.title: Look for wear and damage, every clean
deepSteps.action: With the parts clean, look them over: the extractor and ejector for chips, breaks or wear; the extractor's spring tension; the bolt catch for fouling or looseness; the magazine catch. Inspect the same way after the rifle has been stored a long time.
deepSteps.prose: Each of these is a cause the book's troubleshooting table lists — a broken or fouled extractor or ejector for a stovepipe, a fouled or loose bolt catch for a bolt that will not lock back.
deepSteps.quote: Every time you clean, always inspect for wear and damage and always clean and inspect if your firearm was stored for a long period of time
deepSteps.cite: KRISS DMK Sporting Rifle Series (DMK22C / DMK22C ARCA SWISS) — Owner's Manual — V.01_2023.05.31 — printed on the back page — Cleaning and Inspection, printed p.13

deepSteps.title: Fire control group: one drop at five points
deepSteps.action: With the upper pivoted open, the hammer and trigger are in front of you. One drop of oil at each: the hammer's pivot; the front of the hammer where the bolt meets it; the rear of the hammer where the sear meets it; the front of the sear where the hammer meets it; the trigger's pivot. Do not let the hammer fall while you do it.
deepSteps.prose: One drop is the book's figure. A fouled trigger mechanism is its listed cause for a selector that binds and a trigger that will not reset.
deepSteps.quote: Apply 1 drop of lubricant to the following areas of the FCG:
deepSteps.cite: KRISS DMK Sporting Rifle Series (DMK22C / DMK22C ARCA SWISS) — Owner's Manual — V.01_2023.05.31 — printed on the back page — Lubrication — Fire Control Group, printed p.16

deepSteps.title: The book's stopping point: bolt out, nothing further
deepSteps.action: KRISS recommends a complete teardown, clean and inspection at least every 1,000 rounds, but this book publishes no procedure past taking the bolt assembly out of the upper — no barrel removal, no bolt disassembly, no fire control group removal. Go no further on guesswork. For a problem the cleaning does not cure, the book's contact is a KRISS Certified Dealer or KRISS USA.
deepSteps.prose: This is where the maker's own instructions end.
deepSteps.quote: We recommend a complete teardown, cleaning and inspection at least every 1000 rounds.
deepSteps.cite: KRISS DMK Sporting Rifle Series (DMK22C / DMK22C ARCA SWISS) — Owner's Manual — V.01_2023.05.31 — printed on the back page — Cleaning and Inspection, printed p.13

cleaning.name: BOLT ASSEMBLY
tasks: Lint-free cloth and solvent over every surface of the bolt assembly.
Special attention to the bolt body, the bolt face, the extractor, and the recoil spring and guide.
1–2 drops of oil on the recoil spring and guide.
Several drops on the bolt body, spread to a light film over the whole bolt.

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: Always clean from chamber to muzzle, in the direction of the bullet.

Eyelet adaptor on the bore cable, cotton patch in the eyelet, saturated with solvent. Feed the cable in at the chamber and pull it all the way out of the muzzle. Repeat 2–3 times with a freshly wet patch each time.
Swap the eyelet for the brush adaptor; feed it in at the chamber and pull it through the muzzle 2–3 times.
Patches again, as the first pass, to lift the fouling the brush loosened.

cleaning.name: CHARGING HANDLE
tasks: 1–2 drops of oil on the top and the underside of the charging handle, where it rides on the upper and on the bolt assembly.

cleaning.name: FIRE CONTROL GROUP
tasks: One drop of oil each on the hammer pivot, the front of the hammer where the bolt meets it, the rear of the hammer where the sear meets it, the front of the sear where the hammer meets it, and the trigger pivot.
⛔ Never let the hammer fall with the upper separated from the receiver — it can damage the receiver.
Light film of oil on all metal parts before reassembly or storage, against corrosion.

reassembly: Insert the bolt assembly into the rear of the upper until it is fully seated.
Pivot the upper down onto the receiver.
Push the rear receiver pin back in.
Muzzle in a safe direction — run the function check before the rifle is loaded.
fncheck: Magazine OUT and the rifle confirmed clear first. Pull back the charging handle, point the rifle in a safe direction and, with the chamber empty, pull the trigger: you should hear the hammer release and strike the firing pin. Keep the trigger held, charge the rifle again, then let the trigger out slowly — there should be an audible pop as it resets. Finally put it on Safe and try the trigger: it must be locked and the hammer must not fall. A trigger that does not reset is one of KRISS's listed faults — a weak sear return spring, a fouled trigger mechanism or FCG, or a damaged hammer spring — and if it persists the book sends you to a KRISS Certified Dealer or KRISS USA.
